title: feat(spec)!: reserve the retired callout node types http_request, http_call and webhook; flow-node-http-callout-rename leaves the load path (F5-http of #23543)
body:
Part of #23543
Clause-②: yes (narrowing)

This PR lands family **F5-http** of ruling `6182001882` (item 6), the last family, as the code half. The ADR-0018 dated note is its own Tier H PR, `claude/issue-23543-f5-http-adr-0018-note`, branched from `main`. #23543 stays open for that note and for the save-door question below.

## What

Ruling F5-http A: "`http_request`, `http_call` and `webhook` are reserved inside the open node namespace: the authoring doors refuse them with the rename to `http`; … the entry retires; … `eventType: 'webhook'` on a wait node is untouched."

- **One table, three readers.** `FLOW_RESERVED_NODE_TYPES` and `reservedFlowNodeTypeRefusal` (`packages/spec/src/automation/flow-reserved-node-types.ts`, exported from `@objectstack/spec/automation`) are read by the flow parse, the engine's registration refusal and the conversion itself.
- **The parse refuses each name at the node's `type`**, with the prescription naming `http` and `@objectstack/spec 18`. A top-level node meets a `pattern` per name on `FlowNodeSchema.type`, the `DriverType` (F1) shape, so the generated JSON Schema carries it too (`json-schema/automation/FlowNode.json` `properties.type.allOf` holds the three patterns). A node inside a `loop` / `parallel` / `try_catch` region meets one `FlowSchema` superRefine arm over `collectFlowGraphs`, which skips the top-level graph, so each site is reported exactly once. The open namespace is otherwise unchanged: `http`, a plugin type, a name that merely contains a reserved one (`http_request_v2`, `my_webhook`) and a wait node's `waitEventConfig.eventType: 'webhook'` all parse (pinned).
- **The register side refuses too.** `AutomationEngine.registerNodeExecutor` throws when the executor's `type` or its descriptor's `type` is reserved, and registers nothing; `registerNodeAlias` goes through it. Measured before the change: nothing stopped a plugin registering an executor under one of the names, and the engine is the one executor registry (every builtin and `plugin-approvals` register through it). No node could ever reach such an executor, because an authored node is refused at parse and a stored one is rewritten to `http` first, so the reservation is only true with this door closed (dispatch hypothesis 1, axis ③).
- **The conversion** `flow-node-http-callout-rename` is `retiredFromLoadPath: true`, `retiredAfter: '17.7.0'` (F1 to F4's stamp, still the newest stable under the `18.0.0-next.2` label). Its docblock's "stays on the load path" verdict is rewritten as a retirement record. Fixture unchanged.
- **The conflict guard is removed** (hypothesis 2). Its only purpose was a live third-party executor under a retired name; with registration refused, `reservedNodeTypes` can never contain one, so the guard had no case left. The rewrite is now unconditional. The generic ADR-0078 conflict channel (`ConversionContext.reservedNodeTypes` / `reportConflict`, `onConflict`, the save door's 409) is left in place; see Acceptance notes.
- **Registration:** the D3 entry `flow-node-http-callout-types-reserved` (no `conversionIds`: protocol 11 is below `MIGRATION_SUPPORT_FLOOR`; no `relevantWhen`, so always listed, the F5-jsx shape), the removal-version `JOIN` row (three refusals, one per name), the verdict-list pin (the kept list is now empty and the entry is listed among the retired), and a BREAKING `minor` changeset for `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/service-automation` with FROM → TO, marked `registered flow-node-http-callout-types-reserved`. No `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR` entry (a value retirement, no key) and no `STEP18_RATIONALE` fragment (no step-18 conversion), both the F5-jsx precedent. No `os migrate meta` sentence in the prescription: the removal-version pin's rule would demand `--from 10`, which the CLI refuses.

### The D3 text, tested against the tool

On a temp project with one flow carrying all three names, at this branch's build:

- `os validate`, `os build` and `os lint` exit 1 / 2 / 1, each printing the three refusals at `flows.0.nodes.1.type` / `.2.type` / `.3.type` (the config calls `defineStack`).
- `os migrate meta --from 17` exits 0, applies no edit, prints the three refusals under "Migrated stack does not yet pass schema validation — 3 refusals left after the chain", and lists the D3 entry. `--write` says "the chain made no mechanical change here, so no file was written" and the source is byte-identical afterwards (`cmp`).

The entry's `reason` says exactly that and nothing about the save door.

## Stored rows (hypothesis 5)

A stored flow with an old node type still loads as `http`, pinned at three seams: `stored.test.ts` (`applyConversionsToStoredItem('flow', …)` rewrites all three, unconditionally, a caller's `reservedNodeTypes` naming `webhook` included), `flow-load-conversion.test.ts` (engine rehydration, `registerFlow`), and `nested-region-parity.test.ts` (a `webhook` node in a loop body still runs as `http`, unchanged). metadata-core's artifact door still replays the retired rename inside its window (new case).

## The suites that drove this entry as a live subject (hypothesis 4)

After this PR no real entry is live on the load path (measured: `ALL_CONVERSIONS.filter(c => !c.retiredFromLoadPath)` was exactly this one entry on `main`). Decided per suite; no suite deleted, no assertion weakened.

| suite | what it drove | decision and reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `spec` `conversions.test.ts` | rename cases, the guard, the live-window case, three `normalizeStackInput` sink cases | Rename cases run the data-at-rest posture (`includeRetired`), as the CRUD and F3 cases already do. The guard pair now pins the unconditional rewrite. The live-window case and the three sink cases need a live entry, so they moved, assertion for assertion, to the new `apply-live-window.test.ts`, which appends a test-only probe with `vi.mock` (F2's approach). In their place: a `defineStack` refusal pin and an authoring-funnel-vs-stored-door pin for the retired name. |
| `spec` `region-walk.test.ts` | the walker, through `webhook` | Every pass runs `includeRetired`: the walker's subject is regions, and the stored seams are where a region-nested old node still has to come out canonical. |
| `spec` `stack.test.ts` | `defineStack`'s conversion-notice sink and warn-once | The block moved whole to `stack-conversion-notices.test.ts` with a `vi.mock` probe, so `stack.test.ts` does not mock the registry for its other 1,400 lines. Its two type errors moved with it (cast at the fixture, not ledgered); the `test-typecheck-debt.json` row for `stack.test.ts` shrank by those two. |
| `spec` `stack-conversions-record.test.ts` | the ordering case's second conversion | A second `vi.mock` probe beside the page probe F4 added. |
| `metadata-core` `artifact-forward-conversion.test.ts` | FIRING CONTROL 1 | The probe is appended for that one case to `ALL_CONVERSIONS` from `@objectstack/spec`, the instance the door reads, and removed in `finally`; a premise line asserts no real entry is live. The door itself is the real one. Plus a new case: the retired rename still fires at this door. |
| `cli` `stack-conversion-record-door.test.ts`, `validate-json-strict-exit.e2e.test.ts`, `build-json-failure-conversions.e2e.test.ts`, `validate-json-failure-conversions.e2e.test.ts`, `lint-conversion-notices.e2e.test.ts` | the door's conversion record, `--strict`, failure exits | A spawned CLI is out of `vi.mock`'s reach, so the child loads a test-only preload with `--import` (`test/fixtures/live-conversion-probe.mjs`, the `unbuilt-spec-dist.hook.mjs` precedent). It appends the same kind of probe to `ALL_CONVERSIONS` in both builds of `@objectstack/spec` the child can load (measured: the ESM and CJS tables are two arrays, and a `defineStack` config can load through either). Every real entry stays as published. The record door also gains one case without the probe: `os validate --json` refuses `http_request` by name and records no conversion. |
| `spec` `scripts/build-schemas-check-mode.test.ts` | the entry's `surface` `flow.node.type` as a leaf collider | No change: retirement does not change the entry's surface or remove it. 88 / 88 green. |

The seat's call on F4's open question 2 refused "a test-only entry into the published registry". None is added: every probe lives in a test file or a test fixture outside every package's `files[]`.

## Known gap: the metadata save door (hypothesis 6)

Not touched (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` is outside this family). Measured at this branch with the save-door harness of `protocol.save-flow-canonicalization.test.ts`, saving a new flow whose one node is typed with each name:

| name | with an automation service (a canonicalizer built from the real `applyConversionsToFlow` + `FlowSchema.parse`, the engine's own sequence) | without one |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `http_request` | saved, stored as `http` | saved, stored as `http_request` |
| `http_call` | saved, stored as `http` | saved, stored as `http_call` |
| `webhook` | saved, stored as `http` | saved, stored as `webhook` |
| `http` (control) | saved, stored as `http` | saved, stored as `http` |

So a NEW flow saved through the metadata API with a reserved name is accepted, not refused, against ruling item 6's "the authoring doors refuse them". The door replays every retired flow conversion before judging (the recorded verdict of #4542 / #21982), so this is the same open question F3's release `6205630082` named for every retired flow entry, and it is the seat's to put to the maintainer. The changeset states it in one paragraph rather than claiming a refusal there.

## Readers and examples (hypothesis 7)

No example, skill, hand-written doc or published fixture in this repository authors one of the three names as a node type (`git grep` over `content/`, `skills/`, `examples/`, `apps/`). The one test fixture that listed one as a registry entry, `runtime`'s `http-dispatcher.test.ts` `GET /actions` mock, now lists `http`. Two docblocks this change made false were corrected: `stored.ts` (why flows are not converted by the metadata-protocol seams) and `engine.ts` (`registerNodeAlias` and the rehydration comment). `eventType: 'webhook'` is untouched everywhere.

## objectui (hypothesis 8)

`carrier:` the seat's objectui card at landing. Read sites of the three names at objectui `main` `f78efdd1e3`, identical in file set at the pin `daeb77fc84`: preview samples `apps/console/src/preview-samples.ts:237,244` (two `http_request` nodes); inspector alias `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/flow-node-config.ts:1307` (`http: 'http_request'`) and its `http_request` config group `:771`; canvas cases `previews/flow-canvas-parts.tsx:88-89,261,265,326,330,424`; simulator `previews/FlowSimulatorPanel.tsx:57` and `previews/simulator/flow-simulator.ts:86`; plus `components/src/renderers/basic/metadata-viewer.tsx:271` and the i18n key `engine.flowNode.http_request.label`. `FlowNodeSchema.type`'s TypeScript type is still `string`, so the pinned console build does not break on this change.

## Tests

On the merge head `d5543927` (`origin/main` merged through `os-regen-merge.sh`; no conflict): spec build and `check:generated` "All 14 generated artifacts are up to date"; `@objectstack/spec` test 688 files, 20914 passed (1 todo). On the pre-merge head: spec `typecheck` 0 and `build-schemas-check-mode.test.ts` 88 / 88; `service-automation` typecheck 0 and test 186 files / 2507; `metadata-core` typecheck 0 and test 18 / 737; `runtime` typecheck 0 and `http-dispatcher.test.ts` 248; `cli` typecheck 0 and unit tier 302 files / 4500; `metadata-protocol` save-flow / flow-canonicalizer 34. Re-run on the merge head: the five cli conversion suites 64 / 64 and the two engine files 32 / 32.

**Gates** on `d5543927`: `dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 118, each run with its exit captured before any pipe; `--ran`: "118 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 117 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED". All 117 exited 0, among them `check-adr-0087-registration --base origin/main`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check:spec-changes`, `check:upgrade-guide`, `check:docs`, `check:api-surface`, `check:authorable-surface`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs` and `check:doc-authoring`. The one NOT-MEASURED is `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test`, a shallow-clone prerequisite refusal, declared to CI. Local-only: `check:dev-prereqs` 0, `check:skill-frame-freshness` 0, `check:nul-bytes` 0, `check-platform-checklist --changed-from origin/main` 0.

**Ablation** (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, restored to the HEAD blob each time, `git diff HEAD` empty):

1. The entry's load-path role restored (`retiredFromLoadPath` / `retiredAfter` deleted). Red, 6: the verdict-list pin; the `defineStack` refusal pin; the authoring-funnel-vs-stored-door pin; and three removal-version pins (the `JOIN` row, "every joined entry is a retired conversion", "the joined rows exercise the derivation in both directions"). Spec tests import `src`, so no dist leg.
2. The engine's registration refusal removed. Red, 5: the three per-name refusals, the descriptor case and the alias case.
3. The cli preload dropped from `NODE_OPTIONS`. Red, 2: `lint-conversion-notices`'s two "the fixture REALLY converts" anti-vacuity cases.

## Acceptance notes

- **The ADR-0078 conflict channel has no producer left.** `ConversionContext.reservedNodeTypes` / `reportConflict`, `ApplyConversionsOptions.onConflict`, the engine's `conflicts` array and the save door's `FLOW_CONVERSION_CONFLICT` 409 stay as a generic mechanism, with zero entries using it. Not filed (dead code, zero pull); its retirement would touch `protocol.ts`.
- **One parse reports every site.** Measured: a flow with `http_request` on a top-level node and `webhook` inside a loop body answers both issues in one parse, at `nodes.1.type` and `nodes.2.config.body.nodes.0.type`.
